subject: Operations
title: The Hawthorne Effect
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The Hawthorne Effect.

hook.text: Researchers changed factory lighting. Productivity rose. They reversed it. It still rose. Something else was happening.

buildup.text: The Hawthorne studies ran from 1924 to 1932, testing how conditions affected worker output.

discovery.text: Workers performed better simply because someone was paying attention to them—not because of lighting.

twist.text: The discovery shifted management thinking: social factors and morale matter as much as physical conditions.

climax.text: This launched the Human Relations movement—operations could no longer ignore people's feelings.

punchline.text: Pay attention to workers, and they pay it back.
